content:
STAGE: evidence read (all four bundles) - what constrains the placement
Goal: ground every position in the frozen bundle before ranking.
Read: E5 successor-entropy stratification; E6 width-20 beam survival table; E7 teacher-forced per-position NLL; E8 first-level capacity ceiling vs K; E9 cohort-profile signal; E11 same-first-prefix vs permuted null; E12/E13 geometry statements of each idea.
Observed: baseline l1_br recall@10 0.04671 with gold prefix alive at depth 4 only 0.068 and NLL T1/T2/T3 = 0.00/0.00/0.00, T4 = 9.03 (a degenerate 3-token SID: first tokens trivially predictable, last token near-random). Structured alternatives land 0.0550-0.0636 (l1_br_euclid 0.06207, l1_only 0.06233, resample 0.06363), all below the 0.065 gate. E8 says small K keeps behavioural neighbours together far more often (K=16 0.3106 vs K=256 0.0822, negatives 0.1352/0.0129). E5 says concentration is strongly heterogeneous (top-1 successor mass 0.4375 in the lowest-entropy bin vs 0.0543 in the highest, Spearman -0.973). E11 same-first-prefix 0.0907 against permuted null 0.067.
Reasoning: the evidence rewards COARSE, behaviour-coherent prefixes (E8) and punishes finer/aliased deep partitions (E6 depth-4 survival 0.068, E7 T4 9.03). Any mechanism whose dominant effect is to make L2/L3 cells finer is working against E8/E6; a mechanism that re-aims the level-1 input at the measured behavioural co-clustering quantity is working with E8. That is the axis I rank on, together with inertness risk (E5 says a concentration-scaled step is non-zero for a large, measurable subset; an area-driven rotation may be near-zero for most prefixes).
Still open: relative placement of the two deep-partition mechanisms (behtree vs HSPT).

STAGE: scope and cost check of the four candidates
Goal: confirm each candidate satisfies the five scope items before placing it, and note policy breaches that bear on the rank.
Read: the four SPECIFICATION blocks, COST blocks and RISKS lists.
Observed: all four name a training-only behaviour signal with a computation, an explicit curved operation with a location in training/quantisation, and behaviour-off / curvature-off switches.
- CONCMID-GEO-SID: deterministic pre-quantiser transport b_i = exp_{z_i}(eta_i * sum_j w_ij log_{z_i}(z_j)), eta_i = Herfindahl of the popularity-adjusted successor row; codebooks, loss and encoder untouched; <1% wall clock; switches BEHAV_SMOOTH (eta=0 -> b_i=z_i exactly) and CURV_C (flat RQ + flat blend). Constants derived (kappa = 0.9/max||t_i||, eta measured).
- holonomy-frame-sid: per-prefix frame rotation R_p by minus the hyperbolic area of (o, a_p, b_p) via Gauss-Bonnet, applied to the shared codebook before nearest-codeword assignment, theta=0 when behaviour adds no direction; +5-10% step cost; s = mean||z_i|| derived. Risk it is a near-relabelling and that theta_p clusters to one value.
- behtree-geocut-sid: replaces the RQ partition with a behaviour-cut geodesic tree, prefix-local alphabet, hierarchical CE; +5-15% wall clock plus 5-15 min precompute; documented defaults m=32, fanout<=32, depth 5, 2-sigma null test.
- HSPT-RQ: per-item Lorentz parallel transport of the level-l codebook along the successor direction, rho = ||u|| the accumulated residual; 1.4-1.8x Stage2 cost (571 s -> 780-1050 s); the risk list itself says "rho must be clamped" but no derived clamp bound is given, so a mechanism constant is left to be chosen - a policy problem for a no-sweep round.
Reasoning: no candidate is out of scope, so the placement is on evidence-alignment and one-run robustness, not on admissibility. HSPT carries an underived constant and the largest cost multiplier, which is a policy-exposure penalty on top of its evidence mismatch.
Still open: final order of the middle two.

STAGE: decision on positions 1-2 vs 3-4 and the final order
Goal: fix the ranking with a named piece of evidence per proposal.
Observed + reasoning:
(1) CONCMID-GEO-SID - the only candidate that moves the LEVEL-1 INPUT, i.e. the exact quantity E8 measures. E8: share of canonical pairs whose anchor and target share one of K clusters is 0.3106 at K=16 vs 0.0822 at K=256 (negatives 0.1352 / 0.0129). Pushing each item along the geodesic toward its successors' tangent barycentre is a direct intervention on that co-clustering, and E11 shows the baseline first-prefix agreement is only 0.0907 vs a 0.067 null. Inertness risk is bounded by E5: concentration is strongly heterogeneous (top-1 mass 0.4375 in the lowest-entropy bin over 4,895 items, 0.0543 in the highest), so eta_i is large for a sizeable subset and zero for cold items by construction. Cost is <1% and nothing is optimised, so no collapse mode; E5/E8 both say the signal it uses is real. Best expected value above the 0.065 gate and lowest variance.
(2) holonomy-frame-sid - genuinely curvature-specific (Gauss-Bonnet area -> frame angle, no Euclidean analogue), cheap (+5-10%), and it keeps cell granularity unchanged, so it does not fight E8's "small K wins". It is placed second and not first because E6 shows the baseline failure is concentrated in the deepest token (depth-4 prefix alive 0.068, E7 T4 NLL 9.03) and this idea leaves L1/L2 partitions untouched, while E6's better arms (l1_only 0.06233, l1_br_euclid 0.06207, resample 0.06363) are all still below the gate; if most prefix successor anchors are textually close, theta_p -> 0 and the run reproduces the 0.04671 baseline the idea itself calls inert.
(3) behtree-geocut-sid - its top-of-tree behaviour cuts with fanout<=32 are aligned with E8, but "recurse to depth 5 per SID level, 3 SID levels" permits up to 32^3 leaves for 24,556 items, i.e. near-unique leaves, which is the opposite of the E8 trend (K=16 > K=256) and re-creates the E6 failure (11 items per deepest triple, depth-4 survival 0.068). It also replaces the loss with hierarchical CE plus straight-through reconstruction, the exact combination whose curved-reconstruction form killed the encoder in round one, and it overloads one 256-token vocabulary with prefix-local meanings, which its own risk list admits can make Stage 3 harder to learn. Highest implementation surface, largest chance of a one-run blow-up.
(4) HSPT-RQ - level 1 has rho = 0, so E8's first-level capacity ceiling is untouched; at levels 2-3 it gives each item its own transported codebook, the maximal departure from E8's coarse-cluster finding, with the stated risk that assignment "turns arbitrary" (raised prefix counts, recall below 0.054). It is also the most expensive (571 s -> 780-1050 s), and its unclamped rho with cosh(rho) up to 74 amplifies the along-behaviour component; its own risk list says the clamp must be chosen, which the no-sweep policy forbids. Evidence-wise it makes the worst predicted trade against E6/E7/E8 of the four.
Final order: 1 CONCMID-GEO-SID, 2 holonomy-frame-sid, 3 behtree-geocut-sid, 4 HSPT-RQ.
Still open: nothing; the answer block follows.

ANSWER BLOCK (final record)
RANK: CONCMID-GEO-SID | position=1 | reason=It is the only candidate that moves the level-1 quantiser input, i.e. exactly the quantity E8 measures ("anchor and target share one of K clusters": 0.3106 at K=16 vs 0.0822 at K=256, negatives 0.1352/0.0129), and E11's 0.0907 first-prefix agreement against a 0.067 null shows that level-1 behaviour alignment is the baseline's weakest measurable link; its inertness is bounded by E5's heterogeneous concentration (top-1 successor mass 0.4375 in the low-entropy bin over 4,895 items vs 0.0543 in the high-entropy bin), its step size eta is measured rather than tuned, and with codebooks/loss/encoder untouched at <1% added wall clock it has no collapse path, so it is the best one-run bet on 0.065.
RANK: holonomy-frame-sid | position=2 | reason=E6/E7 localise the failure at the deepest token (gold prefix alive at depth 4 = 0.068, T4 NLL 9.03 with T1-T3 at 0.00) and this is the only candidate that de-aliases that token through a curvature-specific object (Gauss-Bonnet area of (o, a_p, b_p) -> frame rotation, inert in the Euclidean limit) while leaving cell granularity unchanged, so it does not fight E8's small-K result; it ranks below position 1 because it leaves L1/L2 untouched, E6's better structured arms still only reach 0.06207-0.06363 against the 0.065 gate, and its own risk (b) - theta_p clustered by popularity so most prefixes keep theta_p = 0 - would reproduce the 0.04671 l1_br baseline.
RANK: behtree-geocut-sid | position=3 | reason=Its behaviour-cut top levels with fanout<=32 match E8's coarse-cluster advantage, but "depth 5 per SID level, 3 SID levels" allows up to 32^3 leaves for 24,556 items, i.e. near-unique leaves, reversing the K=16 > K=256 ordering in E8 and re-creating the E6 collapse it was meant to fix (11 items per deepest triple, depth-4 survival 0.068); it also swaps in hierarchical CE plus straight-through reconstruction, and it overloads one 256-token vocabulary with prefix-local meanings, which its own risk list concedes can make Stage 3 harder to learn - the largest implementation surface and the highest one-run blow-up risk.
RANK: HSPT-RQ | position=4 | reason=At level 1 rho = 0, so E8's measured first-level capacity ceiling is untouched, and at levels 2-3 a per-item transported codebook is the maximal departure from E8's finding that small, shared K keeps behavioural neighbours together, with its own stated failure mode of arbitrary assignment and recall below 0.054; it is also the dearest arm (571 s -> 780-1050 s, 1.4-1.8x) and its risk list requires an rho clamp whose bound is not derived, a constant the no-sweep policy does not permit, so on E6/E7/E8 it makes the worst predicted trade of the four.
